note.note:
History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
35-year-old male with 3–6 months of poor appetite, fatigue, low mood, ∼1-stone unintentional weight loss, and episodic palpitations/“breathlessness” in elevators; plan is routine blood panel as first-line work-up.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Reduced appetite and energy.  
• Onset/progression: Appetite and energy decline started ~3½ months ago (coinciding with new job). Weight loss began earlier, ~6 months ago. Fatigue and low mood persistent.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Episodic palpitations and feeling unable to breathe mainly when in a lift; no exertional dyspnoea when walking up to ~1 mile (patient has recently avoided walking).  
  – Occasional nausea without vomiting.  
  – Headaches at work.  
  – Decreased libido (“wife complaining about nightly activities”).  
• Pertinent negatives: No chest pain, no diarrhoea, no blood or mucus in stool, normal bowel motions, no acid reflux, no identified food triggers.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Lift episodes precipitate palpitations/air hunger; none others specified.

Past Medical History:
• Primary hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid). Previously treated with levothyroxine; patient stopped therapy several months ago after changing doctor. No recent thyroid function tests reported.  
• No other chronic conditions mentioned.

Medications:
• Levothyroxine – discontinued; last taken several months ago (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• No current medications stated.  
Allergies: Not discussed/recorded.

Social History:
• Occupation: Lawyer; changed to new law firm ~3½ months ago.  
• Exercise: Minimal lately due to feeling unwell.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: Not discussed.  
• Living situation/marital: Married. No additional details.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
Vitals: Not recorded.  
General / systems examination: Not performed (tele-consultation).

Investigations:
• Planned: Routine blood panel (CBC, renal profile, liver enzymes, thyroid function, vitamin levels per clinician).  
• No prior labs or imaging available.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Constitutional symptoms with weight loss, low mood, fatigue, and episodic palpitations likely multifactorial; leading considerations are depressive disorder, relapse of hypothyroidism after stopping levothyroxine, and anaemia. Initial evaluation with comprehensive blood tests arranged.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Major depressive disorder – Supported by persistent low mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, fatigue; no objective cardiopulmonary limitation.  
2. Relapsed hypothyroidism – History of underactive thyroid and medication cessation; compatible with fatigue and mood changes, though weight loss atypical.  
3. Anaemia (iron-deficiency or other) – Could account for fatigue, headaches, pallor (not assessed); bowel normal, making occult GI loss less obvious.

Issue 1: Constitutional symptoms / possible depression
• Assessment: Low mood with somatic features; depression high on DDx.  
• Plan:  
  – Obtain routine blood work to rule out medical contributors (ordered).  
  – Re-evaluate mood once results available; consider PHQ-9 or formal mental-health assessment at follow-up.  
  – Advise patient to seek help sooner if mood deteriorates or suicidal thoughts emerge (safety net).

Issue 2: Possible relapsed hypothyroidism
• Assessment: Stopped levothyroxine months ago; symptoms may relate.  
• Plan:  
  – Include thyroid function tests in blood panel.  
  – If hypothyroid, restart/re-titrate levothyroxine and arrange endocrinology or primary-care follow-up.

Issue 3: Episodic palpitations / situational breathlessness
• Assessment: Likely anxiety-related episodes or panic attacks; cardiac arrhythmia less likely given normal exertional tolerance and lack of chest pain.  
• Plan:  
  – Screen ECG only if palpitations become more frequent/prolonged, develop chest pain, syncope, or sustained dyspnoea.  
  – Advise A&E attendance for new chest pain or severe palpitations (provided in consultation).  
  – Consider anxiety management strategies once medical causes excluded.

General plan items:
• Arrange blood test through Babylon support line; patient instructed on phone number.  
• Follow-up: Automated text to book appointment once results available; earlier review if worsening symptoms.  
• Red-flag advice: Attend A&E for chest pain or significant palpitations; contact service if bowel habits change or vomiting develops.

Quality checks:
● Missing clinically expected elements: Allergies, vital signs, full medication reconciliation, smoking/alcohol history, family history.  
● No direct conflicts between transcript and DDx noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; occasional audio gaps but key data obtained.
